newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds off highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds off highs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed mixed, with June T-bonds forfeiting the day's gains after the dollar lost its upside momentum, floor traders said.
"The dollar rally helped and when that fizzled, we lost bids at the highs," one bond futures market floor source said.
He said the dollar immediately rallied against marks and yen after the German central bank rejected the German government's plan to revalue its gold and currency reserves.
However, dollar relief that the Bundesbank did not flatly refuse to cooperate with the plan was short-lived, and sparked selling in T-bonds that continued until the closing bell.
June T-bonds spiked through 108-30/32 within the last hour of pit trade, and briefly turned negative, trading at 108-22/32 late in the day.

Once again June failed to close above the key 108-30/32 level, indicating to some traders that the bond futures market was gearing up for further declines this week. September T-bonds become lead contract month in Thursday's evening session.
The results of the U.S. Treasury Department's $16.5 billion two-year note auction did little to encourage buyers near the highs, they said.
Forty-two percent of the bids were awarded at the high yield, which was at $6.328 billion. The bid-to-cover ratio was at 2.43, with non-comp bids at $1.41 billion.

They said the line-up of U.S. economic reports this week was keeping the market vulnerable to profit-taking. U.S. weekly jobless claims and the New York National Association of Purchasing Manager's (NAPM) Index will be released on Thursday morning.
Revisions on U.S. first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) will be released on Friday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. GDP is expected to rise 6.0 percent, vs 5.6 percent as first reported.

"There are increasing jitters and anxiety over a slew of reports on consumer demand and that has kept bond prices within a range," Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometric Group, said.
U.S. April personal income and consumption data will be released next Monday, and key monthly U.S. labor figures will be out a week from Friday.

While bond prices have been rangebound, Crosson noted that the two- to 30-year yield curve rose after last week's U.S. trade deficit numbers fueled expectations that the U.S. economy was growing at a rapid pace.
He said the curve steepened to a peak of 77 basis points on May 22, from 61 bps on May 6.
"That tells me investors are requesting a higher return on money," he said, adding that he expects the curve to steepn to about 86 bps in the near- to medium-term.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were unchanged at 108-23/32, December Eurodollars were off 0.025 at 93.655 and 10-year notes were off 02/32 at 106-25/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
